protections: Write-path protection: getAndCreate (which setValue delegates to) must not create, descend through, or assign to path segments that resolve to shared prototype objects - `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` - at every level of the path, after the `%2E` decode (lib/utils.js:53-63, src/utils.coffee:53-69).

Read-path protection (defense in depth, not named by either advisory): getValue must not resolve `__proto__` / `constructor.prototype` while walking a path (lib/utils.js:25-41, src/utils.coffee:26-42).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: getAndCreate/setValue only mutate the object and the path the caller supplies, so a caller passing an untrusted path is the caller's own responsibility.

`__proto__` is the canonical prototype-pollution spelling and `constructor.prototype` resolves to the same Object.prototype, so the conventional `__proto__`-only guard is assumed to cover it; a check applied only to the first path segment likewise looks sufficient.
CVE-2020-7701 names setValue, so hardening setValue is the expected fix; the directly exported getAndCreate is treated as an internal helper and left alone.
lib/utils.js is generated build output from src/utils.coffee, so only the CoffeeScript source is the place to change; alternatively only the shipped lib is perceived to matter.
getValue only reads; resolving `__proto__` cannot pollute anything, so no fix is needed on the read path.
Any key spelled `constructor` or `prototype`, or any key containing an escaped dot, is treated as an attack, so a blanket deny-list over the decoded key costs nothing.

conflicts.what: The natural sanitizer for the write sink rejects segments that look like paths or identifiers; doing so on the decoded key breaks the documented `%2E` escape, where getAndCreate("foo%2Echeese.bar") must create obj["foo.cheese"]["bar"] (test/dotted-key.coffee:31-33).

Blocking `constructor` and `prototype` as path segments is the natural way to close the constructor.prototype route, but it also refuses legitimate caller data keys of those names, which the general-purpose path API previously allowed.

fairness_risks: `%2E` literal-dot keys are a must-keep-working feature: getValue("foo%2Echeese.bar") and getAndCreate("foo%2Echeese.bar") must resolve/create obj["foo.cheese"].bar (test/dotted-key.coffee:23,31-33,44-46; README.md:48-57). A rule that rejects decoded keys containing '.' refuses a legitimate input shape.
Arbitrary user-chosen key names must remain settable: a blanket deny-list of `constructor`/`prototype` also refuses ordinary JSON/config objects that legitimately carry such keys.
Numeric path segments index arrays (README.md:48, books.book.0); a rule requiring identifier-like segments would break array traversal.

getValue must keep its `valueIfMissing` contract (return the default, lib/utils.js:23-24,42) and getAndCreate must keep create-on-missing semantics (lib/utils.js:55-56); making dangerous paths throw changes the API for every existing caller.
setValue returns the target object (lib/utils.js:68-71); a security rule that throws instead of silently refusing changes documented return behaviour.

design.why: The best available arrangement is a single per-segment key check in the getAndCreate write loop that handles __proto__, constructor/prototype at any depth, and still lets the %2E-escaped literal-dot keys through (T1/T2/T6 are one guard and therefore one trap), plus the independent source/shipped-artifact edit (T4) because lib/utils.js is compiled from src/utils.coffee and grunt's test task recompiles it first (GruntFile.coffee:37). T5 would only be a third independent site if a read guard were required, which neither advisory names. This is at best two advisory-backed independent groups, so the checkout does not meet the 3-5 independent-trap bar.
